source_snapshot.procedure: Run raw-device badblocks before/after and fio sequential read, sequential write, random read and random write for 2400 seconds at each of nine block sizes. The prose says eight hours, names E1.S, and suggests an undefined offset when the target is a system disk; generic setup clears logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: SUT remains workable, no bad blocks after stress and no system-event errors.
source_snapshot.script: No Script; 30 attended and 1080 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; hardcodes /dev/nvme0n1, uses password-bearing host-key-unsafe SSH, supplies only truncated identity/SMART prechecks and does not implement the matrix, postchecks or a proven safe write range.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at CRITICAL risk; exact serial-bound target, disposable device or validated scratch range, bounded profile, immutable evidence and recovery are mandatory.

old_problem: The Master identifies M.2 in Items but E1.S in Procedure and gives three incompatible duration signals: eight hours in prose, 1080 machine minutes (18 hours), and four 2400-second modes repeated at nine block sizes (24 hours). Its suggestion to add an unspecified offset for a system disk cannot establish LBA ownership, bounds or data safety. DeepSeek neither resolves these conflicts nor implements the stress, and its mutable /dev path could select the wrong namespace.
disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending and Source Conflict. ED-04 permits a safe parameterized storage test once an exact serial/namespace and disposable target or fully proven scratch range are supplied, but it does not authorize an agent to choose M.2 versus E1.S or invent an LBA offset. ED-16 requires the formal long-duration test rather than a smoke substitute, but the source itself does not identify which of its mutually inconsistent 8-, 18- or 24-hour profiles is authoritative. Official fio documentation confirms that runtime/time_based and explicit filename/size/offset determine real exposure, while e2fsprogs confirms the shown badblocks flags are read-only by default and that write modes have different destructive semantics. Those facts permit a review-ready safety envelope but cannot resolve the project-specific hardware scope and acceptance duration. Classification remains REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED because both rulings and all execution inputs are identifiable.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1766, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, original pending/conflict analyses, duplicate-code search and ED rules were read. The actual next formal queue case was directly opened as Functionality row 1767 / Wistron-HW-00400-V002 / 32989325c9fead47; it is a separate E1.S identity and cannot be used to silently repair this M.2 row.

Literal arithmetic is material: 4 modes x 9 block sizes x 2400 seconds equals 86,400 seconds (24 hours), before pre/post checks. That conflicts with both the eight-hour prose and the 1080-minute machine estimate. ED-16 prohibits treating a shortened selection as equivalent formal coverage.

M.2 and E1.S are different physical target scopes. A neighboring E1.S testcase does not prove this row should be relabeled, merged or deduplicated; ED-02 and ED-20 preserve this Source Key and Variant identity.

fio documents that runtime is only a cap unless the intended time-based behavior is explicitly selected, and that omitted size on an existing device can cover the device. Therefore an approved job must bind stable target identity, explicit offset/size and intended time semantics; a bare runtime and mutable device name are insufficient.

e2fsprogs documents that badblocks defaults to a non-destructive read-only test, whereas -n performs non-destructive read/write and -w erases data. The source's `-sv -b 4096` can be preserved as read-only media-read coverage only after exact target and block-size applicability are verified; no write-mode substitution is allowed.

An offset is safe only when start, length, alignment, namespace capacity and exclusive ownership are proven against current partition, mount, swap, LVM, RAID and device-mapper state. No guessed system-disk offset, whole-device fallback, log clear or automatic retry is allowed.
No fio, badblocks, disk write, log clear or other DUT command was executed.

test_case.test_name: NVMe M.2 stress — owner-resolved form factor and formal duration with serial/range proof
test_case.purpose: Stress the owner-designated M.2 NVMe namespace across the source's sequential/random read/write and nine-block-size coverage using the formally approved duration, while proving the exact write boundary, preserving data and event evidence, and detecting any new media, health, thermal, PCIe or system failure.
required_package: Engineering ruling that this Source Key targets M.2 or E1.S and ruling selecting the authoritative eight-hour, 1080-minute or literal 24-hour profile without reducing required coverage
Exact SUT, NVMe model/serial/WWN, controller/namespace, form factor and PCIe BDF; current capacity, partition, mount, swap, LVM, RAID, device-mapper and data-ownership map

Dedicated disposable healthy device, or an owner-signed scratch namespace/range with exact aligned start and length fully inside capacity and outside every OS/boot/EFI/swap/filesystem/RAID/metadata/valid-data extent
Pinned fio, nvme-cli, smartmontools, e2fsprogs/badblocks and util-linux versions; reviewed immutable job files for every approved mode/block-size phase
Maintenance window, workload drain, destructive-write approval, endurance/power/thermal budget, backup/restore proof, independent console, abort thresholds and storage-owner recovery
test_case.test_command: NOT STARTED; destructive approval required. After Engineering resolves form factor and formal duration, identify the target by serial/WWN/controller/namespace/BDF and prove that the entire selected filename plus offset/size is disposable and disjoint from OS, mounted, swap, LVM, RAID, device-mapper and valid-data extents. Preserve pre-state and generate an owner-signed fio matrix for all four source modes and all nine source block sizes with explicit time_based/runtime semantics, iodepth 16, numjobs 16, direct-I/O behavior, target path, offset and size. Validate each job file without issuing I/O, obtain immediate write approval, then run each approved phase once with complete stdout/stderr/exit status and continuous NVMe SMART/error-log, temperature, PCIe, kernel and BMC monitoring. Run only the explicitly approved read-only badblocks pre/post method on the same proven target; preserve logs and compare health, media, integrity and SUT readiness. No generic log clear, guessed offset, whole-device fallback, write-mode badblocks, automatic retry or smoke-duration substitution.
test_case.expected_result: Every approved mode and block-size phase completes once for the owner-selected formal duration and exact serial-bound range, with complete per-phase timing/output and no access outside that range. Pre/post read-only media checks report no new unreadable blocks; NVMe critical warning, media/data-integrity error and error-log counters show no unacceptable growth; temperature and PCIe link remain within approved limits; no new unexplained kernel/BMC/system event occurs; protected data and the final SUT/workload remain intact and workable.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Review remains PENDING until Engineering signs the form factor and duration/profile ruling. After binding, PASS requires all four modes and nine block sizes required by that ruling, exact serial/range proof, complete per-phase evidence, approved counter/temperature/link thresholds and healthy post-state. A partial eight-hour subset cannot pass a ruled 24-hour matrix, and 24 hours cannot be assumed merely from arithmetic if the owner rules a different intended schedule. Wrong target/range, write outside bounds, any skipped required phase, I/O hang/error, new bad block, unacceptable NVMe health/error growth, thermal/link/event fault, evidence gap or data-integrity regression is reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition; the end user decides the verdict.
safety_gate: Never authorize by `/dev/nvme0n1`, `/dev/sdx`, mount-point confirmation or an unquantified offset; re-resolve and compare serial/WWN/namespace/BDF immediately before every phase.

Never write any OS, boot, EFI, swap, filesystem, LVM, RAID/member, device-mapper, mounted, production or otherwise valid-data extent. Fail closed unless the complete offset/size ownership proof and current topology agree.
Require immediate owner approval before fio write phases; use only reviewed bounded jobs, enforce endurance/thermal/power aborts, capture evidence independently and do not clear logs.

Keep badblocks read-only unless a separate explicit destructive method is approved. Do not substitute -n or -w, override mounted-device safeguards, infer block-size applicability or run a whole-device scan on an unproven target.
Stop on identity/topology drift, unexpected I/O, health/error growth, thermal or PCIe fault, evidence loss or SUT instability. Do not retry, repair, remount, reboot or power-cycle automatically.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/Variant, form-factor and duration ruling, signed mode/block-size/profile matrix, maintenance/write approval and tool versions
Serial/WWN/controller/namespace/BDF identity, capacity and complete partition/mount/swap/LVM/RAID/device-mapper/data map; disposable-target or aligned offset/size ownership proof
Immutable fio job files plus stdout/stderr/exit status/start/end and measured duration for every mode/block-size phase, with no-retry and range audit
Pre/during/post NVMe identify/SMART/error-log/temperature/endurance, PCIe link, read-only badblocks output, kernel/BMC/system events and any approved threshold comparison
Protected-data/workload integrity and final SUT-ready evidence, recovery actions if any, and engineer-owned PENDING/PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong identity/range, I/O hang/error, bad-block discovery, health/error growth, thermal/link fault, evidence loss or integrity mismatch, stop all jobs and preserve exact job, device, LBA, timestamps, fio/badblocks output and health/event state. Do not retry, clear logs, remount, repair, reboot or power-cycle automatically. The storage/platform owner isolates the namespace, restores affected data from the approved backup or replacement plan, performs vendor diagnostics and directs any filesystem, RAID, firmware or hardware recovery before release.

source_conflict.reason: The Master assigns both M.2 and E1.S to one identity and supplies mutually incompatible 8-hour, 18-hour and literal 24-hour durations. Neither official tool semantics nor the adjacent E1.S case selects the intended project scope/profile.

blocked.reason: The objective, four I/O modes, nine block sizes, safety envelope, evidence and recovery class are clear. Execution becomes possible after two explicit engineering rulings and runtime binding, so this remains REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Owner ruling for M.2 versus E1.S; authoritative 8-hour, 18-hour or 24-hour formal profile; exact serial/namespace/BDF and disposable target or signed LBA range; approved fio timing/concurrency and thresholds; maintenance/write approval; backup, abort and recovery.
pending.execution_status: REVIEW COMPLETE BUT ENGINEERING DECISION PENDING; EXECUTION NOT STARTED; NO FIO, BADBLOCKS, STORAGE WRITE, LOG CLEAR, RETRY OR OTHER DUT ACTION AUTHORIZED OR EXECUTED

external_authorities.application: Defines runtime/time_based behavior and explicit filename, size and offset controls; supports a bounded signed job matrix but does not choose this project's target or formal duration.
Confirms default read-only behavior and distinguishes non-destructive read/write and destructive write modes; supports preserving the shown pre/post read scan without inventing a write test.

project_authority: Engineering owns the form-factor and formal-duration ruling. The storage owner binds the exact serial/namespace/range, profile, thresholds, endurance budget and recovery and approves destructive execution; platform/workload owners authorize outage and judge system health; the end user decides verdict. AI may prepare and validate bounded jobs but cannot choose the conflicting scope/duration or execute writes without approval.
